rationale: The assistant identified the correct cause (flashing clock after power cut locking out heating) in the very first reply and the customer fixed it with no part or engineer, matching the ground truth exactly. Weaknesses: it told the customer to 'check your manual if possible' right after they said they had none, never asked make/model to give precise button steps (the customer had to volunteer 'Neff'), and the third reply largely re-explained the same flashing-clock cause and 'look for a button with a clock icon' instruction, frustrating a customer who had already said they could not identify the buttons. A hedged aside that 'the control panel may be faulty' was premature but not asserted as diagnosis. Overall a well-served homeowner with a safe, correct, no-cost resolution.
